name: Question 18
problem:
The resting heart rate of a group of adults is normally distributed with a mean of $\mu \,\text{bpm}$ and a standard deviation of $8\,\text{bpm}.$ Additionally, $70%$ of the adults have a resting heart rate between $0.9\mu \,\text{bpm}$ and $1.1\mu \,\text{bpm}.$ Find the percentage of adults with a resting heart rate lower than $70\,\text{bpm}.$ **Round your answer to two decimal places.**

*Hint: A table of values of ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ for different values of $p$ is given below, where $p=Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

worked_solution:
Let $X$ represent the resting heart rate of a randomly selected adult. Then we have $X∼N(\mu ,{8}^{2}),$ and we want to find $P(X<70).$ But first, we need to find the mean $\mu .$ 

We know that $P(0.9\mu <X<1.1\mu )=0.70.$ First, we convert this to a cumulative probability:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0.9\mu <X<1.1\mu ) & =0.70 \\ 2P(\mu <X<1.1\mu ) & =0.70 \\ P(\mu <X<1.1\mu ) & =0.35 \\ P(X<\mu )+P(\mu <X<1.1\mu ) & =0.5+0.35 \\ P(X<1.1\mu ) & =0.85\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we convert $X$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<1.1\mu ) & =0.85 \\ P(Z<\frac{0.1\mu }{8}) & =0.85 \\ Φ(\frac{0.1\mu }{8}) & =0.85 \\ \frac{0.1\mu }{8} & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.85).\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, 

$$
{Φ}^{-1}(0.85)=1.0364.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{0.1\mu }{8} & =1.0364 \\ 0.1\mu  & =8.2912 \\ \mu  & =\frac{8.2912}{0.1} \\  & ≈82.912.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can solve for $P(X<70)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<70) & =P(Z<\frac{70-82.912}{8}) \\  & ≈P(Z<-1.61) \\  & =Φ(-1.61) \\  & =0.0537 \\  & ≈5.37%\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, approximately $5.37%$ of the adults have a resting heart rate lower than $70\,\text{bpm}.$
